summary:
West: a 99-long, flat-topped rose temple (white_terracotta on a polished_granite podium, calcite/quartz frieze and cornice) symmetric about x 50, with end pavilions, 8-column pedimented porticos north and south, rows of glass skylights and a shallow stepped weathered-copper dome to y 26.
East: Pei's trapezoid cut into two triangles. Blank planar walls to y 14, five flat parallelogram towers to y 20 including the 18° knife-edge prow at (108,33), a dark entrance slot in an H-shaped west face, and a glowing triangular space-frame atrium.
They read as these buildings by the long low pink temple with its green dome, and by the sharp triangular towers in the same marble. West Building: long pink white_terracotta temple on a granite podium, two 8-column quartz porticos with pediments, a low copper dome on a drum, and skylight strips on a flat roof. East Building: a planar trapezoid in two triangles with five prismatic towers, a knife-edge prow, a dark entrance slot and a glass atrium space frame.
Interiors are hollow and lit by flush froglights, with shroomlight uplights at the bases. elements.md and the plan.md PALETTE, VOCABULARY, ROOMS and PARTS sections are written. The `$MCD blocks --check` output was only partly read: I saw calcite_stairs and white_terracotta_stairs flagged unknown and avoided them.

West shell: West shell built in parts/west-shell.mjs: granite podium and quartz floor, hollow walls round the union of spine and pavilions (attic to y14, central block to y16), rotunda partitions at x40/60, N/S/E/W door recesses and four niche panels. make.sh reports no refusals and no off-palette blocks.
polish: The roof tool's cleared-cell count was never checked: make.sh says it cleared 174 shell cells above the eave. They are probably the central block's z 9/30 wall cells at y 14..16 under the porticos, but I did not confirm that. If the centre attic looks notched, the roof part should check it.
Check says 15 floating smooth_quartz blocks at y 11 (for example 44,11,2 and 43,11,37) along the portico fronts. They are not in this part's cells, so the roof part should look at them.
I only looked at one render tile (front-left), so the end-door hoods and niche panels are not checked by eye.
The rotunda partitions at x 40/60 are closed walls. The drum part must open the rotunda upward, and any gallery link needs a note in plan.md.

I built the terrace and portico podium (z 3..8, z 31..36 for x 42..58) as solid to y 3 with a smooth_quartz top, so the portico floor is already there. The north/south steps at z 0..2 and z 37..39 are left for the roof part.

waste.what: Wrote a union-footprint wall loop by hand, because marbleWall only does single rectangles. Overlapping outlines would leave interior walls and refused writes where spine and pavilions meet.
waste.cost: about 20 lines of loop, plus checking edge cells and niche exclusions by hand
waste.tool: marbleWallUnion(g, boxes, {tall, exclude}) in h1.mjs: walls on the perimeter of a union of rectangles, with per-box heights and carve-out predicates

waste.what: Door recesses for the two end doors, 2 wide at z 19..20, plus hoods, were done by hand because recessDoor takes only odd widths.
waste.tool: recessDoor with even widths and an optional hood slab

companions.task: Check the niche panels and pilaster seating on the finished shell, and look at the central-block attic corners.
Check the tinted_glass door backs and the end-door surrounds and hoods against the renders.

summary:
West roofs, porticos, dome: West roofs part built in parts/west-roof.mjs: spine, pavilion and central decks with eight skylight strips, two Ionic porticos (16 columns, architrave, cornice, steps with footing), pediments, a drum ring, a stepped copper dome and the oculus lantern.
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt. My part wrote 3846 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette; `$MCD fit` is OK.
The roof spec (roof.json, temple) is laid by runParts after the shell, not by this part. Eight W-items in elements.md are ticked (W6–W10), and the notes are in plan.md.
polish: Portico return-column architraves (x 43 and 57 at z 6 / z 33) and cornice stairs at the corners are not built; only the front row is.
Cornice stairs use the straight shape; the outer-corner shape is not set.

`$MCD check` reports 15 FLOATING smooth_quartz cells at (x 43..50, y 11, z 2) and (x 43..49, y 11, z 37), plus 16 orphans at x 41 and 59 (z 3..7 and 33): none placed by this part, so probably the roof tool's overhang or eave. Not verified; the roof part or the trim part should check it.

The architrave row at y 11 and the portico columns rely on the shell's floor at y 3 and the roof's eave at y 13; the pediment cells may be partly refused by the roof (not in the report; no refusals were printed for this part).
Architrave and cornice have no portico lamps (shroomlight under the floor, lanterns on the step posts): those belong to the trim/lights part.

waste.what: Derived the drum ring, central deck, dome discs and cornice ring by hand from the circle rows, and copied CIRCLE rows and an inDisc helper into the part.
waste.cost: about 40 lines of coordinate logic written and debugged; one wrong sed edit and two reruns
waste.tool: vocab helper exporting the circle-row disc test (inDisc / ring between two radii) and a drum() helper that builds the drum ring, its base and cornice in one call

waste.what: Wrote a local ionicColumn because the vocab helper puts a bottom slab under the shaft, which fit flags on all 16 columns.
waste.tool: fix ionicColumn in vocab/h1.mjs (full-block base, quartz pillar, top-slab capital) so every portico uses the same column

waste.what: Footing under the wide steps was computed by hand from groundAt for each cell.
waste.cost: about 60 cells of footing set one by one
waste.tool: slabSteps with an automatic footing option (fill from groundAt up to the step's base)

waste.what: Checked the result by reading the rendered tile and running check and fit separately, not from one report.
waste.tool: a single mcd part-check command that prints the part's own refused, floating and fit lines

companions.task: The column bases, capitals and steps: the footing and the step treads, so the Ionic columns stand on full blocks and the half-steps are cut properly.
Check the roof tool's overhang at the portico eaves (z 2 and z 37, y 11) and the temple gable that the pediment sits in; the floating cells are his to fix.
The portico uplights (shroomlight in the podium top between the columns) and the lanterns on the step posts; that is the trim part, so the handover is the portico floor at y 3.

summary: West trim and lights: West trim built: 40 pilasters, y 12 cornice ring, y 15/17 coping, portico lanterns and 6 hanging lamps. make.sh saves a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes.
polish: W12 partial: portico and podium shroomlights not built (shell fills those cells). Standing lanterns at y 4 stand in; (48,4,36) refused.
Step-head lanterns at x 41 and 59 not built (step cells are the shell's).
Drum pilasters not built (roof part owns the drum ring, locked before this part).
Cornice corners are one-cell gaps at convex diagonal corners.
Not mine: smooth_quartz floating at y 11 along z 2 and z 37 (x 43..50), with orphans at x 41 and 59.

waste.what: Pilaster placement written out call by call, with each wall-cell offset worked out by hand.
waste.tool: A pilasterRow(g, {xs, wallZ, face}) helper, or positions from the FACADES table in base.mjs.

waste.what: Cornice and coping outline walked by hand because corniceRing takes one rectangle and would cut into the pavilions.
waste.tool: corniceRing accepting a list of masses with a portico skip-set, plus a coping walk on the same outline.

waste.what: Finding locked and unsupported cells with node probes and rebuilds.
waste.tool: A column dump (mcd occupancy --box) and runParts printing locked cells before each part.

companions.task: Plan the portico and podium light before the shell is laid: flush shroomlights in the podium top at y 3 and the podium face at y 1.
Shape the cornice ring's convex corners with outer-corner stair shapes.

summary:
East shell and towers: East shell (parts/east-shell.mjs): solid planar body rows (y 0..14), flat-topped towers with the knife-edge prow tip at (108,33), the atrium court carved out (y 1..14 empty for part 5's glass), the entrance slot with tinted back and hanging lanterns, recess and wedge paving, and the dark bands (recess, south y4/y10, north diagonal y10).
make.sh saves a whole build.nbt; the East part places 18,478 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette. Aerial render reads as the trapezoid with towers and the prow.
Plan.md PARTS 4 and elements E1–E6 are ticked, and a Notes line records the shell decisions.
polish: Part 5 (roofs/atrium): the body's y 13 calcite course from planarWall is the body roof, so the bottom-slab deck at y 13 will be refused there; the deck belongs on the towers only (y 19, inside the y 20 coping).
Tower interiors are open from y 15 to 19 with no deck (part 5 lays the y 19 decks); the body interior is solid to y 14, so the towers' interior air above the body is visible from above until then.
Atrium glass at y 14..15 and the ribs/pyramids are part 5's (E7); the atrium's y 0 floor is marble from planarWall and the froglight grid is part 5's.
Entrance slot: entranceSlot carves y 0..4 to air, so the slot has no floor block at y 0 (the old lawn cell is gone); part 6 (grounds) should pave the slot floor or the walk into it.

Not checked: $MCD fit / walk for the East (no rooms.json East rooms); mcd check reports no floating or unsupported East blocks (its 15 floating and 18 orphan reports are all West-part cells at y 11, z 2 and z 37).
Recess and wedge paving uses smooth_sandstone at the ground's top (groundAt), so it can sit at y 1 under some wedge cells rather than the plan's y 0; the grounds part should match it.

waste.what: Transcribed the BODY and TOWER x/z ranges from plan.md by hand into [z, x0, x1] rows, including the recess exclusion for z 9..21 and the ranges for z 16..26 and the prow.
waste.cost: about 60 range rows typed by hand and cross-checked against plan.md's tables twice; one mistake caught in review (a stray ternary)
waste.tool: A plan-table parser (or a plan.json to rows helper) that turns plan.md's BODY and tower tables into [z, x0, x1] rows directly, and applies the recess and slot exclusions by name, would have removed the transcription step.

waste.what: Worked out the wedge cells (open cells of z 27..33 beside the prow) and the atrium triangle's rows by hand.
waste.cost: about 30 cells computed mentally; solidCells() was written to derive wedge cells from the body and tower footprints
waste.tool: vocab helper that returns the open cells of a plan zone (wedge, recess, atrium) as rows, so no worker re-derives openings from the footprint.

waste.what: Checked the East part by rendering tiles and writing a custom aerial view (--view) by trial, since the shared tiles only frame the whole site at the street.
waste.cost: two renders, one aerial camera guessed by hand
waste.tool: mcd render --zoom-plot 1 or a per-plot preset camera (plot centre, golden-hour aerial), so each plot's part can be judged without guessing a camera.

waste.what: zsh does not word-split a MCD variable holding 'node path', so the first mcd call failed and needed a rerun.
waste.tool: A plain mcd shim on PATH (or the Bash tool's shell set to bash) so the documented $MCD variable works as written.

companions.task: The entrance slot's tinted-glass back, the dark gray_stained_glass bands on the south face and the north diagonal, and the tinted glass at the slot's far wall: the glazier sets and checks glass lines flush with the wall planes.
The knife-edge prow: the 18-degree tip at (108,33) running unbroken y 0..20 with no trim, and the prow/SE tower edges, which must stay razor-sharp at the coping.
The three hanging lanterns in the entrance slot ceiling and the lamp posts along the East plaza, so the slot glows at dusk and no dark cell is left at the entrance.

summary:
East roofs and atrium: East roofs and atrium is built in parts/east-roof.mjs: the atrium glass space frame at y 14 (ribs, pyramids at y 15), tower decks (smooth_stone_slab bottom at y 19 inside each tower's coping), and interior lights (atrium froglights at y 1, four hung lanterns under the spine ribs, one froglight in each tower).
make.sh saves a whole build.nbt; this part places 397 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette. In isolation the roof pieces float (the shell is not yet merged); the render shows them sitting on the east plot.
elements.md E7 and E8 and plan.md PARTS 5 are ticked, with notes.
polish: The body is solid marble to its calcite coping (planarWall fills every body cell from y 0 to 14), which contradicts plan.md's hollow FLOORS table. Body froglights every 6 cells cannot be placed and the body interior is not hollow. Owner decision needed, not fixed here.

The atrium glass at y 14 and its ribs are refused if the East shell's planarWall writes calcite at y 14 over the atrium cells. The shell must leave the atrium void (x/z rows of ATRIUM, y 1..15) empty. Check the merged build's parts-report.

The tower deck at y 19 and the atrium roof float in this isolated build because the East shell is not merged yet. They should rest on the shell's perimeter walls and body in the merged build; confirm with mcd check there.
The atrium froglights stand at y 1 on the atrium floor (the shell's floor at y 0 is locked), so they are 1-high obstacles in the atrium walk. Acceptable for an unwalked void, but flagged.

waste.what: Hand-typed the atrium triangle rows and the five tower footprints, and worked out the tower interior cells (all four neighbours inside the footprint) and the froglight grid cell by cell.
waste.cost: about 40 coordinate rows typed and checked by eye; one retry on the spread syntax for the tower rows
waste.tool: A vocab helper such as towerDeck(g, rows, y) that places the bottom-slab deck and returns the interior cells, plus a plan.md ROWS table for the atrium and tower footprints that generators can import directly.

waste.what: Checked the froglight and lantern positions against the atrium triangle and rib lines by hand.
waste.cost: a few dozen mental checks; no retries needed
waste.tool: atriumRoof could return its rib cells, and hangLamp could take a row list, so lamps are placed under ribs without recomputing the mod-4 lines.

companions.task: Fit the atrium space frame: set the glass panes, the light grey rib lines and the raised pyramid panes at the crossings, once the atrium's shell opening is confirmed.
Plan the atrium and tower interior lighting from a light-level map (mcd light) so the atrium glows at dusk with no dark floor cell.

summary:
Grounds and lighting: Grounds and lighting (parts/grounds.mjs) built: smooth_sandstone walks along the north and south faces, the plaza between the buildings and the East paving, all laid only on untouched grass.
Lamp posts every 10 blocks along the walks, plus a greedy lawn cover over both plots (79 posts); the light map at y 1 has min 3, mean 8.6, zero dark cells.
make.sh saves a whole build.nbt; my part reports 1308 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; G1 ticked in elements.md, note added to plan.md Notes.
polish: The floating smooth_quartz at y 11 (x 43..50, z 2 and z 37) and the dangling orphans at x 41/59 are West roof/portico architrave cells that are not built yet (earlier parts' responsibility, not mine).

The whole-build walk check reports walkable end to end: false (narrowest 0, along x); the north and south approaches depend on the portico steps and the porticos from the West roof part, so I did not change them.
Only the street-level render was reviewed. The hero aerial view of the plaza and lamp rhythm has not been checked by eye.
Edge slabs (smooth_sandstone_slab) on the walks, worn dirt paths and planting were not built; the plan does not require them.

waste.what: Checked by hand whether each walk/lamp cell was free: first pass refused 4 lamp writes at the south door recess, because carved air counts as written but isAir() reads it as free.
waste.cost: one failed make.sh run and a rebuild (about 2 minutes)
waste.tool: A build-library helper such as `g.isFree(x,y,z)` (or a `runParts` query for 'written by an earlier part, air included') so parts don't have to guess the lock rule from g.get()===undefined.

waste.what: Found the dark lawn cells by reading the ASCII light grid row by row and counting columns to place the extra lamps.
waste.cost: about 3 reads of a 150-column text map, plus one rewrite of the lawn pass
waste.tool: `mcd light --dark-cells --json` (or `mcd light --cover <step>`) that lists dark floor cells as coordinates and proposes lamp spots to clear them.

waste.what: Hand-wrote the paving and lamp layout as nested loops over plan rectangles, with per-cell checks for grass-at-top and air-above.
waste.cost: one generator module (~90 lines) and two iterations
waste.tool: A `pave(g, box, block, {onlyGrass: true})` and `lampGrid(g, box, {every: 10, lamp})` pair in vocab, so ground parts are a list of boxes.

companions.task: Check the lantern spacing against the light map and say which posts can drop out of the greedy cover without leaving a dark cell.

Plant the lawn edges (trees and shrubs along the Constitution Avenue and Mall walks, a worn dirt_path across the lawn) and set smooth_sandstone_slab edges along the walks. The plan does not ask for these, so they were left out.

summary: inspection: walk ok and fit OK, nothing to fix
